focal_organ: Cirsium flower head: stigma/pollen/disc vs involucral bract wall vs young closed bud
contrast: Different antagonists need not traverse same defence interface: anatomical route and reproductive stage jointly determine which putative defence can matter.

original_sources.route: eggs inserted among florets of recently opened heads
original_sources.gate: exposed floret field rather than necessarily penetrating phyllary barrier
original_sources.source: Vanbergen et al. 2006 Journal of Animal Ecology DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2656.2006.01099.x
original_sources.plant_fit_effect: larvae feed on receptacle and achenes; no specific effect of spines/angle on egg placement demonstrated

original_sources.route: females chew oviposition punctures through phyllaries of flower heads; scars on phyllaries
original_sources.source: Gijsman et al. 2020 Global Ecology and Conservation 22 e00945, DOI 10.1016/j.gecco.2020.e00945
original_sources.plant_fit_effect: infested heads 60% fewer mature seeds; secondary/tertiary heads suffer higher infestations than terminal; correlational infestation comparison not randomized actual spine effects

original_sources.route: adult females deposit eggs in maturing buds; larvae burrow into reproductive tissue and induce seedhead gall
original_sources.source: University of Idaho / IBiocontrol 2024 Introduced Thistle Agents
original_sources.plant_fit_effect: seedhead galls reduce seed yield; no spine-orientation field manipulation

original_sources.consumer: multiple seed predator types and legitimate pollinator arthropods
original_sources.route: legitimate pollinators do not contact sticky traps; some seed predators avoid trap
original_sources.gate: sticky involucre exudate may be spatially bypassed
original_sources.source: Thomas 2007 The Great Lakes Entomologist DOI 10.22543/0090-0222.2188; Thomas 2003 DOI 10.22543/0090-0222.2085
original_sources.plant_fit_effect: neutralizing sticky traps did not increase seed predation or decrease seed production in 2003 study

original_sources.consumer: Tephritis conura, Xyphosia miliaria, Pteromalus elevatus
original_sources.route: two tephritid species feed within the heads; shared parasitoid probes the capitula to reach larvae
original_sources.gate: shared capitulum substrate, different host insect responses to habitat
original_sources.phenophase: T. conura June–July feeding; parasitoid peak oviposition August; X. miliaria season dependent
original_sources.source: Vanbergen, Hails, Watt & Jones 2006 Journal of Animal Ecology DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2656.2006.01099.x
original_sources.plant_fit_effect: 20 woodland sites; 10 grazed and 10 ungrazed, T. conura and shared parasitoid P. elevatus more abundant with grazing; X. miliaria unaffected; parasitism of T. conura about 2x in grazed habitat. No trait-specific spine/angle manipulation or direct seed rescue.

functional_prediction.H0_spatially_partitioned_no_conflict: If pollinators arrive from disc and outer defences are never encountered by them, there may be NO pollination-vs-defence cost. Antagonists entering via exposed florets may also bypass bract armature. Morphological correlations do not imply functional tradeoffs.
functional_prediction.H1_phyllary_barrier: Direct real spine/phyllary access-gaps should preferentially change head-wall chewer/ovipositor success on buds, not necessarily floret-layer tephritid access during anthesis.
functional_prediction.H2_orientation_stage: Natural nodding orientation rotates the outer wall in world coordinates, altering route-conditioned successful entry only if arthropods use gravity-referenced strategies. The same head's opening phase is a separate predictor.
functional_prediction.H3_time_enemy_shield: After initial infestation, larger mechanical access barriers may obstruct parasitoid attack, but only pre-damage host killing can benefit viable achene production.
functional_prediction.H4_alternative: Head size and position select buds suitable for weevil oviposition; rain/UV and pollen presentation shape fitness, independently of insect access.
functional_prediction.H5_within_same_plant_guild_heterogeneity: An identical capitulum cannot be assumed to give identical protection against all tephritids: T. conura responds to grazing/habitat and X. miliaria does not in Vanbergen et al. 2006. Control species identity before inferring a generic seed-feeder barrier.

new_identifiability_requirement: Each observed arrival must be classified as approaching exposed florets, phyllary exterior, phyllary interstice, receptacle base, or stem.
Stage-conditional head position and real measured phyllary opening/spine rigidity/direction must be independently verified.
One head and plant biological unit, with approach-level events nested in effort-calibrated observation bouts.
Do not conflate interspecific route contrast with within-population adaptive selection, independently evolving lineages or common treatment outcome.
Test effective pollen contacts, confirmed adult oviposition and independently validated pre-damage parasitoid effect before seed fate.
Within a single nominal guild, retain consumer species/host identity and distinguish each parasitoid-host pair. A single 'seed predator' slope ignores documented within-plant differences.
claim_ceiling: Evidence for different antagonist access portals across existing Cirsium studies, NOT evidence that any measured Cirsium spine orientation phenotype evolved adaptively to route partitioning.
